# Step 2: Analyze schemas and target columns
# Target columns:
# ['batsman': string,
#  'batsman_runs_x': integer,
#  'batsman_runs_y': integer,
#  'no of balls': integer,

#  'total_runs': integer]

# Observations:

# Assigning:
# df0.batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_x

# df4.batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_x_4

df2_renamed = df2.rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_y'})
df3_renamed = df3.rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_y_6'})
df4_renamed = df4.rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_x_4'})

# Merge with df4 (which has additional columns 'no of balls' and 'strike')

# Merge with df1 (which has 'total_runs')
final_merge = pd.merge(merge_all_runs, df1, on='batsman', how='outer')

int_columns = ['batsman_runs_x', 'batsman_runs_y', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs_x_4', 'batsman_runs_y_6', 'total_runs']
float_columns = ['strike']

# Fill NaNs

            final_merge[col] = 0.0
        elif col == 'batsman':
            # batsman must exist, but just in case
            final_merge[col] = ''

output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_35/target_multisource_cot.csv"
